decisions.reason: As a flagship tied to the firm's announced sustainability direction, management is inclined to keep justifying the investment despite two years of non-observation, though the absence now makes withdrawal a real possibility.

This multi-model foldable container line fits the core reusable-packaging business and carries substantial sunk development and marketing commitment, so management would still tend to persist and treat weak visibility as temporary or portfolio repositioning.

With only modest original promotion and no later website presence, this crate has too little visible commitment to overcome four years of underwhelming evidence, making discontinuation the more likely choice.

Although it sits in the firm's core pallet offering, the rackable pallet lacked strong public prominence and after two unobserved years management would be more willing to redeploy resources away from it.

Its dedicated page and broader product-line status imply meaningful prior commitment, so management would still be somewhat prone to continue backing it and explain weak results as niche-market timing.

The stand-alone launch created some commitment, but as a more specific single product that has since disappeared from view, it is easier for management to let go than the more central or broader lines.
